bib.title: GLM: General Language Model Pretraining with Autoregressive Blank Infilling
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2022), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 320-335

question: Can one pretraining framework perform well on NLU, conditional generation and unconditional generation, where BERT, GPT and T5 each lead on only one?
hypothesis: Autoregressive blank infilling with span shuffling and 2D positional encodings, varied in number and length of blanks, yields one model that matches or beats BERT, T5 and GPT of the same size and data.
contributions: GLM: autoregressive blank infilling pretraining with 2D positional encodings and arbitrary span order
Multi-task pretraining by varying number and length of blanks (document-level, sentence-level)
NLU tasks reformulated as cloze questions answered by autoregressive generation (PET-style, multi-token answers)
Outperforms BERT, T5 and GPT at same size/data; best single model at 1.25x BERT-Large parameters

method.summary: A single Transformer is pretrained by masking continuous spans (each replaced by one [MASK]), then generating the spans autoregressively in random order with Part A bidirectional and Part B causal attention plus 2D positions. Multi-task variants add document-level or sentence-level long-span objectives. NLU is fine-tuned as cloze questions with verbalizers and cross-entropy.
method.task: autoregressive blank-infilling pretraining; evaluated on SuperGLUE, GLUE, SQuAD, summarization, question generation, text infilling, language modeling

models.name: GLM Base
models.architecture: Transformer, same as BERT Base; pre-LN reorder, single linear output layer, GeLU

models.name: GLM Doc / GLM Sent
models.architecture: Large size, multi-task with document-level or sentence-level objective

models.name: BERT Base/Large, UniLM Large, T5 Base (220M)/Large (770M), BART Large, RoBERTa Large, GPT Large, BLM, MASS, BERTSumAbs, UniLMv2 Base, SemQG

other.GPT Large: trained by authors with same data and tokenization as GLM Large

training.objective: Eq 1: max_theta E_z~Zm [sum_i log p(s_zi | x_corrupt, s_z<i)]; spans length ~ Poisson(lambda=3), resampled until at least 15% of tokens masked; multi-task adds document-level (single span, length uniform 50%-100% of original) or sentence-level (full sentences covering 15% of tokens); in a batch short and long spans sampled with equal chances

other.fine-tuning NLU: cloze question + verbalizer, cross-entropy; single-token tasks score = logit of verbalizer token, multi-token = sum of log-probs; fine-tuning hyperparameters for SuperGLUE not stated
other.seq2seq fine-tuning (Gigaword, SQuAD QG): 4 epochs, AdamW, peak lr 3e-5, 6% warmup, linear decay, label smoothing 0.1
other.infilling fine-tuning: 5 epochs, AdamW, peak lr 1e-5, 6% warmup linear, dynamic masking
other.BERT baseline: BERT Large reproduced with authors' implementation, data and hyperparameters

inference.decoding: Gigaword: beam search size 5, repeated trigrams removed, length penalty tuned on dev; QG: beam size 5, length penalty tuned on dev; samples (App D): top-k random sampling
inference.prompting: NLU cloze patterns of Table 8 with a single [MASK]; zero-shot LM for LAMBADA/BookWiki

metrics.name: LAMBADA accuracy
metrics.definition: teacher forcing; correct only if all subword tokens of final word are correct

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests reported.
Compares to T5 not directly because data and parameter counts differ (authors concede).
GLM RoBERTa trained for only 250K steps due to resource limits; Stories dataset replaced so not identical to RoBERTa data.
Document-level objective slightly hurts NLU and conditional generation; GLM Large alone cannot do language modeling (ppl > 100).
Zero-shot LM numbers are given only in Fig 4.
Fine-tuning hyperparameters for SuperGLUE not stated.
Generated samples (App D) contain factual errors.

terms.definition: Spans of the input are replaced with [MASK] and the model predicts the missing tokens autoregressively, given the corrupted text and previously predicted spans.
Each token has two positional ids: position in the corrupted text, and intra-span position (0 for Part A, 1..span length for Part B).
